source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Diabetic ketoacidosis should still be evaluated because SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis may occur with glucose below 250 mg/dL.","B":"Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state is established by the glucose value of 210 mg/dL without additional testing.","C":"Hypoglycemia is the likely metabolic emergency because SGLT2-related ketoacidosis requires glucose above 300 mg/dL.","D":"The symptoms can be attributed to medication intolerance without checking ketones or acid-base status at this glucose level."}}
source_row.rationale: FDA warns that ketoacidosis with SGLT2 inhibitors may occur with blood glucose below 250 mg/dL. Compatible symptoms should prompt assessment for ketones and metabolic acidosis rather than dismissing DKA because glucose is only modestly elevated.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions §5.1 — Ketoacidosis; evaluate compatible symptoms regardless of presenting blood glucose. Revised 01/2026; live DailyMed label currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring, reconciliation and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client taking an SGLT2 inhibitor presents with nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, and fatigue. The blood glucose is 210 mg/dL. Which complication must still be considered?
